claim: Triton orbits Neptune opposite to Neptune's spin, the only large moon to do so, and scientists think it is a captured Kuiper Belt object.

beats.caption: Opposite to Neptune's spin
beats.vo: Neptune spins one way. Its moon Triton circles it the other way. Astronomers call that a retrograde orbit.

beats.caption: The only large moon that does this
beats.vo: And it's the only large moon in our solar system that does this.

beats.caption: A captured Kuiper Belt object?
beats.vo: Moons born alongside their planet follow its spin. A backwards one suggests an outsider. Scientists think Triton was a Kuiper Belt object, captured by Neptune's gravity millions of years ago.

beats.caption: Pluto's cold cousin
beats.vo: That fits. Triton looks a lot like Pluto: sixteen hundred eighty miles wide, with a frozen nitrogen crust, and a surface around minus three hundred ninety-one degrees Fahrenheit.

beats.caption: Captured world. Wrong-way orbit.
beats.vo: Voyager 2 even caught active geysers there in 1989. So Triton is likely a captured Kuiper Belt world, circling Neptune the wrong way. Where do you think it came from?

sources.text: NASA Science, Triton: https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/moons/triton/ (retrograde orbit, only large moon to do so, captured Kuiper Belt object, 1,680 mi diameter, -391 F surface, Voyager 2 geysers 1989)
